references.text: Gray hair is a crown of glory that is gained by living righteously—both texts highlight the honor due to the elderly.
The beauty of young people is their strength, and the glory of old age is gray hair—emphasizing respect for the aged.
With the aged comes wisdom, and with length of days comes understanding—showing why the elderly deserve respect.
Elihu waited to speak because the others were older than he—an example of practical respect for the elderly.
The same chapter contains a similar exhortation to fear God in connection with treating others rightly.
You shall fear the Lord your God—reiterating the command to fear God as motivation for right conduct.
Honor all people, love the brothers, fear God—linking reverence for people with the fear of God.
Paul exhorts Timothy to treat older men as fathers—showing how respect for the elderly continued in the early church.
Honor your father and your mother—the foundational command to honor the elderly within the family.
Fear your mother and your father—the same chapter links respect for parents with the fear of God.
